summary: The specific concern flagged for this file — that a heavily-read ahkam passage might be quietly issuing fiqh rulings — does NOT hold. There is no niyyah ruling, no suhur/iftar timing ruling, and no free-standing fatwa. The one exemption statement (fidya for the very old and the incurably ill) is explicitly attributed to al-Muyassar and matches the paired report verbatim ("كالشيخ الكبير، والمريض الذي لا يُرْجَى شفاؤه"); the ayyaman ma'dudat discussion explicitly flags al-Tabari's recorded ikhtilaf; and the qul-absence reading is openly labelled a balāghī inference with al-Muyassar's contrary implied-qul gloss named. Every checkable tafsir attribution matches the report: al-Tabari's sabab (near-to-whisper vs far-to-shout), Ibn Kathir's Abu Musa hadith, al-Muyassar's al-qurb al-lā'iq bi-jalālihi, al-Tabari's shahr/shuhra sword etymology, al-Muyassar's 'seek the children Allah decreed', al-Tabari's ṣiyām = al-kaff. All five yas'alūnaka cross-references (2:189, 2:215, 2:219, 2:220, 2:222, 20:105) are accurate. Morphology 49/49 verified; all Arabic exact. The one genuine MODERATE is the false universal in the scholarly_note. NOTE — REPORT DEFECT, not a content error: in tafsir-report-183-187.md the Ibn Kathir block for 2:184 is a byte-identical repeat of the 2:183 block, and the Ibn Kathir + al-Muyassar blocks for 2:220 are byte-identical repeats of 2:219's.

issues: [MINOR] "Al-Muyassar says Allah will show Hell to the disbelievers until they behold it clearly." — 'until they behold it clearly' is al-Tabari's phrasing in the paired report ("حتى يروها ويعاينوها"). al-Muyassar's actual block reads "وأبرزناها لهم لنريهم سوء عاقبتهم" — brought forth to show them the evil of their outcome. Repeated later as "Al-Muyassar's phrasing emphasizes that Hell is shown to the disbelievers so they behold it." Compatible in substance, wrong label.

'Brought near' is uzlifat, which in 26:90 is said of the Garden for the muttaqīn, not of the Fire. The referent (the ghāwūn) is right; the verb gloss is swapped.

summary: No CRITICAL. Arabic verified exact (verify_arabic 1/1); morphology 4/4. The core analysis is sound and checks out: 'arda IS a cognate verbal noun (maf'ūl muṭlaq) intensifying the verb; 18:48 IS the passive وَعُرِضُوا of the same root and IS in the paired report; 18:57's akinnah/waqr is quoted correctly and is in the report; al-Tabari's gloss ("وأبرزنا جهنم ... فأظهرناها للكافرين") is reproduced accurately. All external cross-references verify: 79:36 (burrizat al-jahīm li-man yarā), 89:23 (wa jī'a yawma'idhin bi-jahannam), 102:5-7. The old CRITICAL is unsupported.

issues: [CRITICAL] "**The Quran preserves exactly one prayer of Nuh in his own words — and it is the one that was refused.**" — False, and it is the thesis of the entire article (title, hook, Element One, Theme One, closing invitation, du'a all rest on it). The Quran quotes Nuh's own words repeatedly: 23:26 قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ; 26:117-118 قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى كَذَّبُونِ / فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ; 54:10 فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ; 71:26-28; 11:47. All verified via canonical-verse.mjs.

[CRITICAL] "One transcript kept, and it is a refusal. One answer kept, and the transcript is gone." / "Allah has given us, across two surahs, both of Nuh's prayers." — The configuration the article says does not exist occurs twice, verbatim and adjacent: 26:117-118 (quoted prayer) is answered in 26:119 فَأَنجَيْنَـٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ; 54:10 (quoted prayer) is answered in 54:11 فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ. summary: ESCALATE MODERATE → CRITICAL. Everything the rebuild notes asked to be verified holds; the thesis they were built around does not. What verifies: karb occurs exactly 4x in the Quran (6:64, 21:76, 37:76, 37:115 — confirmed by a full 6,236-ayah scan of the validator corpus); al-karb al-'aẓīm occurs exactly 3x, at precisely 21:76 / 37:76 / 37:115; naṣara + min rather than 'alā is correct and the two Surah Hud parallels are real (11:30, 11:63); al-Jalalayn's gloss is verbatim in the paired report — ﴿ونَصَرْناهُ﴾ مَنَعْناهُ ... أنْ لا يَصِلُوا إلَيْهِ بِسُوءٍ — as are al-Jalalayn on nādā (دَعا عَلى قَوْمه بِقَوْلِهِ ﴿رَبّ لا تَذَر﴾) and on ahlahu (الَّذِينَ فِي سَفِينَته), and al-Muyassar on ahlahu (المؤمنين به) and naṣarnāhu (مِن كيد القوم). Form claims are corpus-confirmed: nādā III, najjaynāhu II, fa-stajabnā X. The 950 years (29:14) and fingers-in-ears (71:7) are accurate. What fails is the load-bearing claim that the answered prayer's words were 'sealed' and that only a refused prayer survives in Nuh's own voice — a claim the Quran contradicts in four places and the file's own Ibn Kathir block contradicts directly. NOTE — REPORT DEFECT, not a content error: the al-Tabari blocks for both 21:76 and 21:77 are the same offset block on 21:75 (Lut, 'وأدخلناه في رحمتنا'), truncated.

issues: [MODERATE] "The pronoun *minhu* — from him, from it — reaches back across three ayahs to the *nuṭfah*, the drop." — Stated as settled and turned into a rhetorical set-piece ("the distance between almost nothing and the entirety of human civilization"), but both tafsirs available for 75:39 in the paired report read the pronoun as the human being, not the drop: al-Tabari — "فجعل من هذا الإنسان بعدما سوّاه خلقا سويا أولادًا له، ذكورا وإناثا"; al-Muyassar — "فجعل من هذا الإنسان الصنفين: الذكر والأنثى". The mani reading is a genuine classical option, so this is false certainty rather than a false claim, but the file gives no sign that its own sources read it the other way.

[MODERATE] "Imam al-Shafi'i, one of the greatest legal minds in Islamic history, built an entire argument on this single word ... From one word at the end of one ayah, al-Shafi'i derived the entire necessity of Shari'ah." — Inflation presented as fact and then re-used in Theme 1 ("This is what Imam al-Shafi'i saw in sudā") to carry a theodicy argument. What is actually attributed to al-Shafi'i in the tafsir tradition is the one-line lexical gloss of sudā as lā yu'maru wa lā yunhā — the same gloss the file separately and correctly credits to al-Tabari. No source is given for the systematic derivation, and nothing in the paired report supports it.

The Step 0 grounding table hedges correctly ("I impf 3fs passive (or IV passive)"), and the reader-facing prose only says 'passive', which is right — so this is confined to shipped scaffolding.

summary: The old CRITICAL is not supported. Arabic verified exact across all 14 tagged references including the 75:3 and 75:4 ring-opening quotations (verify_arabic 14/14); morphology 20/20. Every reader-facing form claim is right: sawwā IS Form II, yuḥyiya IS Form IV (corpus: Hyy, IV), qādir IS an active participle, yaku IS apocopated from yakun, yutraka and yumnā ARE passive, dhālika IS the distal demonstrative. The central sudā gloss is verbatim al-Tabari from the paired report ("أن يترك هملا أن لا يؤمر ولا ينهى، ولا يتعبد بعبادة"). Two genuine MODERATEs remain: an interpretive referent presented as fact against both of the file's own tafsirs, and an inflated al-Shafi'i attribution. NOTE — REPORT DEFECT, not a content error: in tafsir-report-036-040.md the Ibn Kathir block is byte-identical across all five ayahs 75:36-40 and is offset — it is the commentary on 75:26 (كَلاَّ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِىَ), truncated. This file's Ibn Kathir coverage is therefore effectively absent, which is why the al-Shafi'i gloss could not be checked against it.
